traceability.evidence:
1) Test Execution (Core Functionality, Integration, Error Handling, Test Setup) - I ran the full test suite with verbose output via `npm test -- --verbose`. - All 40 test suites and 302 tests passed. - Relevant passing suites for this story: - `tests/plugin-setup.test.ts` - "Traceability ESLint Plugin (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)" - ✓ `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] plugin exports rules and configs` - ✓ `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE][REQ-NPM-PACKAGE] plugin exposes meta with name, namespace, and version` - `tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts` - "Plugin Default Export and Configs (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)" - ✓ `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] default export includes rules and configs` - ✓ `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] rules object has correct rule names` - ✓ `[REQ-RULE-REGISTRY] configs.recommended contains correct rule configuration` - ✓ `[REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM] configs.strict contains same rules as recommended` - ✓ `[REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY] configs.recommended maps valid-annotation-format to warn and others to error` - ✓ `[REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY] configs.strict uses same severity mapping as recommended` - `tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts` - "Flat config presets integration (Story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG)" - Validates that the plugin's `recommended` and `strict` configs work correctly with ESLint v9 flat config, covering **REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT** and **Integration** acceptance criterion. - `tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts` - "Traceability ESLint Plugin Error Handling (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)" - ✓ `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] should report error loading rule and provide placeholder rule` - `tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts` - "CLI Error Handling for Traceability Plugin (Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP)" - ✓ `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING] should exit with error when rule module missing` - Multiple other tests validate rule registration, configuration, and TypeScript-based rule implementations, satisfying **REQ-RULE-REGISTRY**, **REQ-TEST-SETUP**, and **REQ-TYPESCRIPT**.
2) Core Plugin Structure and Rule Registry (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM) - `package.json`: - `"main": "lib/src/index.js"` and `"types": "lib/src/index.d.ts"` expose a standard Node.js module entrypoint and TypeScript typings, matching **REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE** and **REQ-NPM-PACKAGE**. - The plugin is built from TypeScript via `"build": "tsc -p tsconfig.json"`, confirming **REQ-TYPESCRIPT**. - The `files` array (`"lib", "README.md", "LICENSE", "SECURITY.md", "user-docs", "CHANGELOG.md"`) ensures only built code and docs are published, aligned with npm package best practices. - Tests `plugin-setup.test.ts` and `plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts` both assert that: - The plugin exports a `rules` object and `configs` object. - The default export and named export both include rules and configs. - The `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` objects contain the correct rule configurations (rule registry & configuration system). - This demonstrates that **REQ-RULE-REGISTRY** and **REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM** are implemented and verifiably correct.
3) ESLint v9 Flat Config Compatibility (REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, Integration AC) - `tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts` (which passed) explicitly validates: - `[REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS] recommended preset enables traceability rules via documented usage`. - `[REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS] strict preset also enables traceability rules via documented usage`. - This test suite uses ESLint v9 flat config APIs to load and run the plugin, confirming that: - The plugin exposes flat-config-compatible `recommended` and `strict` presets. - The plugin integrates cleanly into an ESLint v9 flat-config environment. - Together with the successful test run, this satisfies **REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT** and the "Integration" acceptance criterion.
4) Error Handling (REQ-ERROR-HANDLING, Error Handling AC) - `tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts`: - Confirms the plugin handles failures when loading a rule module by reporting an error and providing a placeholder rule instead of crashing ESLint. - `tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts`: - Ensures the CLI exits with an error and a useful message when a rule module is missing. - These tests are tagged in their descriptions with Story 001.0 and `[REQ-ERROR-HANDLING]`, and they all passed in the last run, so the plugin meets the error-handling acceptance criterion and **REQ-ERROR-HANDLING**.
5) TypeScript Implementation and Test Infrastructure (REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-TEST-SETUP) - `package.json` devDependencies include `typescript`, `ts-jest`, `@types/eslint`, `@typescript-eslint/utils`, `@types/jest`, and `jest`. - `scripts` include: - `"build": "tsc -p tsconfig.json"` (TypeScript compilation), - `"type-check": "tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json"`, - `"test": "jest --ci --bail"`. - Numerous tests under `tests/rules/*.test.ts` and `tests/config/*.test.ts` validate the plugin rules using Jest and ESLint APIs (and, by implication, RuleTester-style behavior), fulfilling **REQ-TEST-SETUP**. - The presence of TypeScript tooling and the compiled `lib/src/index.js` entrypoint confirm that the source is written in TypeScript and built into JavaScript for consumption, satisfying **REQ-TYPESCRIPT**.
6) npm Package Structure and Plugin Discovery (REQ-NPM-PACKAGE) - `package.json` fields relevant to npm publishing and plugin usability: - `"name": "eslint-plugin-traceability"` (conventional ESLint plugin naming), - `"main": "lib/src/index.js"`, `"types": "lib/src/index.d.ts"`, - `"files"` scoped to `lib` and key docs, - `"peerDependencies": { "eslint": "^9.0.0" }` for proper ESLint integration, - `"engines": { "node": ">=18.18.0" }` for runtime compatibility, - `"repository"`, `"bugs"`, and `"homepage"` for npm metadata. - These align with best practices for a publishable npm ESLint plugin and satisfy **REQ-NPM-PACKAGE**.
7) Documentation and User Experience (Quality Standards, User Experience, Documentation ACs) - `package.json` includes `"files": ["README.md", "user-docs"]` ensuring user-facing docs are part of the published package. - The story explicitly references: - `docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md`, - `docs/custom-rules-development-guide.md`, - `user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md`, - `README.md`. - These files exist in the repo (verified by file search in previous cycles) and are referenced by tests like `flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts`, which validates documented usage. - The presence of a dedicated `user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md` and README usage examples, combined with passing integration tests based on those docs, demonstrates that the plugin can be installed and configured with clear instructions, satisfying the **User Experience** and **Documentation** acceptance criteria and the "Quality Standards" bullet.
8) Overall Definition of Done - All referenced tests for this story and its dependencies pass. - The package is TypeScript-based, buildable, and testable, with CI-oriented scripts and Jest test infrastructure in place. - The plugin exports rules, configs, and meta, is compatible with ESLint v9 flat config, handles errors gracefully, and is packaged correctly for npm publication. - Documentation for setup and plugin development exists and is wired into tests and publishing.
Based on this concrete evidence, every acceptance criterion and listed requirement (REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE, REQ-ESLINT-COMPAT, REQ-RULE-REGISTRY, REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM, REQ-NPM-PACKAGE, REQ-TYPESCRIPT, REQ-TEST-SETUP, REQ-ERROR-HANDLING) is satisfied by the current implementation.
